summary.text: Nikki Budzinski is the Democratic U.S. Representative for Illinois's 13th District, first elected in 2022, and won re-election on November 3, 2026, according to unofficial results.

A Peoria native and University of Illinois graduate, she worked in the labor movement, the Illinois governor's office and the federal Office of Management and Budget before running for Congress. She serves on the Agriculture and Veterans' Affairs committees.

paragraphs.text: Budzinski was born in Peoria, Illinois, and earned a bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.
According to her House biography, she joined the labor movement after college and worked on wages, benefits and workplace safety for firefighters, grocery workers and meatpackers.
She worked on the campaigns of Chris Dodd, Hillary Clinton and J.B. Pritzker, and was president of Budzinski & Partners, LLC, a political consulting firm.

Budzinski later served as a senior advisor in the Office of the Governor of Illinois, where she chaired the Broadband Advisory Council; her House biography says she also led negotiations on raising the state minimum wage to $15 an hour.

She then served as chief of staff of the federal Office of Management and Budget, where, her House biography says, she helped implement the American Rescue Plan and establish the Made in America Office.
Budzinski won the Democratic primary over David Palmer on June 28, 2022, and the November 2022 general election over Republican Regan Deering, and she took office in 2023.
She won re-election in the November 3, 2026 general election with 62.6% of the vote to Jeff Wilson's 37.4%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
She serves on the House Agriculture and Veterans' Affairs committees and is Ranking Member of the Veterans' Affairs Subcommittee on Technology Modernization.
She founded the Congressional Postal Service Caucus, and serves as a Vice-Chair of the Congressional Labor Caucus and as Vice Chair of Policy for the New Democrat Coalition.
